title: Students protest RSS leader's presence at Central University of Kerala seminar

tea.why: Students protested against a seminar on Vande Mataram, alleging it was part of a "saffronisation agenda" and featured RSS-linked speakers.
tea.want: Protesters demanded universities offer equal ideological space and avoid becoming platforms for political agendas.
tea.changed: Oct 6: Four students were injured in clashes with police during the protest at the university.

summary: On October 6, 2026, student organizations including SFI, NSUI, MSF, and AISF protested at the Central University of Kerala in Kasaragod. The protest targeted a national seminar on Vande Mataram, which students alleged was part of a "saffronisation agenda" due to the participation of individuals with ideological links to the RSS, such as J. Nandakumar of Prajna Pravah. Protesters demanded that universities provide equal space for all ideological viewpoints and not serve as platforms for political agendas. Police prevented students from entering the seminar venue, leading to clashes where four students were reportedly injured. The Leader of Opposition, Pinarayi Vijayan, condemned the police action.
demands: Universities provide equal space to all ideological viewpoints
Universities should not be turned into platforms for political agendas
response: Police prevented students from entering the seminar hall, leading to a confrontation. Students alleged that police assaulted them and tore their clothes. The Leader of Opposition, Pinarayi Vijayan, condemned the police action against the students.

updates.text: Student organizations including SFI, NSUI, MSF, and AISF protested at the Central University of Kerala against a national seminar on Vande Mataram.
Protesters objected to the seminar's title, organizers, and speakers, particularly J. Nandakumar, whom they linked to the RSS.
Police prevented students from entering the seminar hall, leading to clashes on campus.
Four students were injured during confrontations with police, with students alleging physical assault.
Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan condemned the police action against the students.
